skill.name: research
skill.description: Delegate broad, read-only investigations to local subagents. Receive concise conclusions with supporting file paths, symbols, caveats, and unknowns.
skill.summary: Keep the primary context focused by delegating noisy research and receiving evidence-backed conclusions.
skill.author: warpdotdev

content.value_statement: Large investigations can flood the primary agent context with irrelevant files and logs. This skill delegates read-only research and returns concise conclusions with cited evidence.
actual_capabilities: Delegates broad, read-only codebase investigations to local subagents.
Chooses single or parallel delegation based on whether research questions are independent.
Guides subagents to inspect large diffs, logs, stack traces, and symbol usage.
Requests distilled conclusions with exact file paths, symbols, caveats, and unknowns.
Keeps raw investigation noise outside the primary agent context.
limitations: Requires an environment that can spawn local subagents.
Adds latency and token usage compared with direct inspection.
Does not replace direct file reading when edits require the underlying material.
Recommended model names may be unavailable or change across platforms.

use_cases.title: Trace a complex test failure
use_cases.description: Delegate inspection of long CI logs and related code, then receive the likely cause with supporting locations.

use_cases.title: Summarize a large pull request
use_cases.description: Review a substantial diff through a subagent and receive the main changes, rationale, risks, and evidence.

use_cases.title: Survey an unfamiliar architecture
use_cases.description: Map how a component or API is used across a repository without loading every inspected file into primary context.
use_cases.target_user: Architects and developers joining a project

prompt_templates.title: Answer a repository question
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate {question} in {repository_path}. Work read-only. Return a concise answer with exact file paths, symbols, and important caveats.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused answer from an unfamiliar repository.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {log_or_test_failure} and trace the relevant code. Identify the root cause, cite supporting locations, and note anything not verified.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer needs signal from long logs or stack traces.

prompt_templates.title: Review a large change
prompt_templates.prompt: Research {pull_request_or_diff}. Summarize behavioral changes, affected components, design rationale, risks, and tests. Support each major conclusion with file locations.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs a compact assessment of a large change.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate independent investigations
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate these independent areas in parallel: {area_one}, {area_two}, and {area_three}. Synthesize the results, preserve evidence, and identify cross-area uncertainties.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user has several independent repository questions.

output_examples.input: Find the root cause of this failing integration test and cite the relevant implementation and test locations.
output: Root cause: The retry handler converts the timeout into a permanent failure.
Evidence: The report identifies the handler and failing test locations.
Caveat: External service behavior was not reproduced locally.

output_examples.input: Summarize this large pull request, including behavior changes, risks, and test coverage.
output: Change: The request pipeline now validates credentials before loading account data.
Risk: Existing clients with incomplete credentials may fail earlier.
Coverage: Unit tests cover validation, but migration behavior remains untested.

output_examples.input: Explain how session recovery works across the repository and identify the main call sites.
output: Flow: Recovery starts after connection loss, restores persisted state, and reconnects active sessions.
Evidence: The summary lists the coordinator, persistence layer, and reconnect entry points.
Unknown: Concurrent recovery behavior requires runtime verification.

best_practices: Provide an exact question, repository path, and suspected files or symbols.
Keep investigations read-only unless the task explicitly requires changes.
Request concise conclusions, exact evidence locations, caveats, and unresolved questions.
anti_patterns: Do not delegate a single lookup or a few known file reads.
Do not delegate when the primary agent must edit the same files immediately.
Do not split one coherent investigation into artificial parallel tasks.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when investigation requires many files, long logs, large diffs, or broad repository surveys.

faq.question: When should I inspect files directly?
faq.answer: Inspect files directly for small lookups or when you need their contents for immediate edits.

faq.question: Does the skill modify repository files?
faq.answer: The workflow is read-only by default. A task must explicitly request changes before a subagent should modify files.

faq.question: Can it run several investigations at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Parallel subagents are appropriate only when the questions are independent and do not require shared intermediate findings.

faq.question: What should a research report include?
faq.answer: It should include a direct answer, exact evidence locations, relevant symbols, caveats, and unresolved questions.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Local subagent availability still depends on the host environment.
